title: Tenant reservation decay: telemetry hardening and gradual reclamation plan
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: During the 2026-03-08 hosted API capacity incident we observed prolonged GPU pool exhaustion despite autoscaler activity. Investigation revealed that per-tenant reservation state created by the admission controller was not decaying correctly when tenants became inactive. The result: reservations persisted longer than intended, reducing available slots and causing queue buildup and higher tail latency for best-effort tenants. This ticket tracks follow-ups: a gradual reclamation algorithm to avoid eviction storms, telemetry and alerting improvements to detect reservation leakage earlier, a synthetic simulation harness to validate behavior under mixed workloads, and a cautious rollout plan with canary gating and rollback criteria.

Scope: Changes touch the admission/reservation service, autoscaler interactions, telemetry/metrics ingestion pipeline, and the hosted-api incident runbook. Work is limited to server-side control plane and runtime admission; no client SDK changes required.

Goals:
- Eliminate multi-minute reservation leakage for inactive tenants.
- Reduce false negatives in capacity alerts by improving metric granularity and aggregation cadence.
- Ensure reclamation does not trigger mass evictions; reclaim in measured increments with tenant-informed grace windows.
- Validate changes via deterministic simulation and production canary.

Non-goals: Re-architecting autoscaler or changing pricing model. This ticket focuses on correctness and observability fixes only.
root_cause_summary:
A regression in the reservation TTL decay path introduced in runtime-1.19 caused per-tenant reservation entries to skip scheduled decrement events when the admission service instance was resharded. The stale entries continued to consume logical slots; combined with an unusual spike in long-running embedding requests, GPU pools hit exhaustion. Telemetry aggregation was configured with a 60s rollup which delayed detection of rising reservation occupancy, preventing early preemptive scaling.

Contributing factors: a) resharding race in the admission service, b) reservation TTLs tuned conservatively (long), c) metrics rollup too coarse, and d) admission fallback did not implement gradual reclamation (it attempted bulk ejection in previous POC, but we disabled it due to an earlier outage).
action_items: Mateo Rivera - 2026-03-21 - Implement gradual reclamation algorithm in admission service: reclaim up to 5% of reserved slots per 30s per pool with prefer-low-priority-first. Include soft-grace tag and metrics (reclaims_initiated, reclaims_succeeded, reclaim_failure_reason).
Anika Shah - 2026-03-18 - Patch reservation TTL decay during reshard: fix missed scheduled tasks and add resilience for instance handoff. Add unit tests covering reshard scenarios.

Kai Nguyen - 2026-03-20 - Telemetry hardening: change reservation occupancy metric to 10s rollups, add per-pool 1m and 5m sliding windows, emit histogram for reservation age distribution. Update Grafana panels and alert rules.

Sofia Patel - 2026-03-22 - Build deterministic simulation harness that can replay mixed tenant workloads (short text gen, long embed runs) to exercise reclamation and autoscaler interactions. Include chaos scenarios for reshard.

Grace Li - 2026-03-25 - Canary plan and runbook: add gating checks, safety thresholds, rollback criteria, and automated abort if reclaim rate > 25% or error rate increases > 2x. Integrate into deployment pipeline.
Infra Oncall - 2026-03-28 - Post-rollout 72h monitoring: run targeted dashboards and collect incident log bundles for review.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests cover reshard handoff and TTL decrementing edge cases.
Simulation harness demonstrates no more than 10% slot loss from stale reservations across 10k-tenant mixed workload scenarios.
New metrics (reservation_age, reservation_reclaims_{initiated,succeeded}) are emitted and visible on dashboards with 10s granularity.
Canary rollout with 3% traffic shows stable latency and no customer-visible errors for 72h; rollback triggers validated and exercised.
Post-deploy incident runbook updated with new detection thresholds and remediation steps.
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Patel: Initial triage notes - incident started at 03:12 UTC. We observed GPU pool 7 at 100% utilization with >2000 queued requests, autoscaler had added nodes but available logical slots remained low. Reservation table snapshot showed many entries with age > 15m.

2026-03-11 Mateo Rivera: Found resharding code path where scheduled decrement tasks are registered with instance-local timers that can be dropped when ownership migrates. Draft fix in branch 'fix/reservation-timers'.
2026-03-12 Kai Nguyen: Metrics team agrees to change rollup cadence. We'll need to instrument backlog and reservation_age histograms; estimate 2 days to get end-to-end.

2026-03-13 PM review (Liam O'Connor): Prioritize gradual reclaim algorithm over aggressive eviction; customer experience is paramount. Also requested canary gating and a playbook update before prod rollout.

2026-03-14 Sofia Patel: Simulation harness prototype runs completed: in 1:1 reproduction we reproduced slot leakage when reshard occurs mid-request. Next: add reclaim policy simulation and tune reclaim window.
notes: Risk: incorrect reclaim parameters could cause short-term increased latency for reclaimed tenants. Mitigation: conservative reclaim rate, canary, and immediate rollback thresholds. Operational playbook to include a temporary tenant amnesty endpoint to quickly release reservations for manually-verified tenants if needed.
